description:
This image displays two panels of false-colour satellite imagery with overlaid yellow polygons, illustrating the issue and resolution of multipart geometries in Natura 2000 (N2K) terrestrial sites. The background imagery shows dense vegetation as red, and bare ground or rock as light blue/white. Small cyan points are present within the polygons.

The top panel shows a Natura 2000 site boundary (yellow polygon) where the geometry is fragmented into multiple disconnected parts, including smaller, isolated yellow outlines within the larger extent of the protected area. This visualises the problem of "multipart geometries".

The bottom panel shows the same geographic area with the yellow polygon boundaries refined. The smaller, isolated polygons depicted in the top panel have been processed and integrated into a more contiguous and geometrically consistent boundary, representing the resolved state of the multipart geometry issue. The cyan points remain in similar locations across both panels. No scale bar, compass, legend, or explicit reference year is visible in the image, but the surrounding document context refers to "2021_PUM_v1" and mentions consistency with Minimum Mapping Unit (MMU) requirements.
